skill.name: file-organizer
skill.description: Organizes local files and folders by analyzing directory contents, identifying duplicates, proposing folder structures, and carrying out approved cleanup steps.
skill.summary: Plan and run approved local file organization tasks with duplicate checks and cleanup guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, network exfiltration, or runtime code was found. Static alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline path examples, and ordinary prose in SKILL.md. The skill documents optional local filesystem commands and requires approval before destructive cleanup.

remediation.issue: Shell examples can be copied into a live terminal without a dry run.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the confirmation rule and add dry-run or preview steps before move, rename, archive, or delete actions.

remediation.issue: Markdown command fences triggered static scanner noise.
remediation.suggestion: Label command blocks as examples and keep placeholder paths explicit so users do not mistake them for automatic execution.

content.user_title: Organize Files with Clear Cleanup Plans
content.value_statement: Messy folders make files hard to find and increase storage waste. This skill analyzes local folders, proposes safer structures, and performs only approved cleanup actions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews local directory structure and summarizes file counts, sizes, and types.
Groups files by type, purpose, age, project, or archive status.
Finds likely duplicates by hash, filename, or file size.
Proposes new folder structures before changing files.
Moves, renames, and archives files after user approval.
Provides cleanup summaries and maintenance tips.
limitations: Requires local filesystem access through the host assistant tool.
May need user judgment for ambiguous file names or sensitive folders.
Approved move or delete actions can affect real files.
Duplicate commands may vary by operating system and installed tools.

use_cases.title: Clean a Downloads Folder
use_cases.description: Sort recent downloads into documents, images, installers, archives, and items that need review.

use_cases.title: Restructure Project Directories
use_cases.description: Separate active work from archived projects and apply consistent naming across project folders.

use_cases.title: Prepare Files for Archiving
use_cases.description: Identify old files, duplicate copies, and folders that should move to a long-term archive.

prompt_templates.title: Start with one folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup of a single messy folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize my Downloads folder. First show the current file types, then propose a conservative plan. Ask before moving or deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Find duplicates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup focused on storage waste.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicate files in my Documents folder. Group duplicates by confidence, recommend which copy to keep, and ask before deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Review project structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Projects directory. Separate active work, archives, and templates. Keep current work untouched and provide a step-by-step move plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a maintenance workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recurring process for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a recurring cleanup process for my home directory. Include folders to scan, naming rules, archive thresholds, and confirmation points.

output_examples.output: A cleanup plan lists documents, images, installers, and archives, then asks for approval before moving files.

output_examples.input: Find duplicates in my Documents folder.
output_examples.output: A duplicate report groups matching files, compares dates and sizes, recommends the best copy, and marks deletions for confirmation.
A project plan separates active work from archives, suggests clearer names, and records each proposed folder move.

best_practices: Start with one folder and review the proposed plan before approving changes.
Archive uncertain files before deleting them.
Keep active work, reference files, and archives in separate folders.
anti_patterns: Do not organize an entire home directory without a clear scope.
Do not approve deletions until duplicate groups and paths are reviewed.
Do not move sensitive or active project files without checking exclusions.

faq.question: What does this skill organize?
faq.answer: It helps organize local folders such as Downloads, Documents, project folders, photos, and archives.

faq.question: Will it delete files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the assistant to ask for confirmation before deleting files.

faq.question: Does it upload my files?
faq.answer: No evidence found. SKILL.md describes local filesystem review and does not include network upload instructions.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I start safely?
faq.answer: Start with one low-risk folder, review the plan, and keep backups for important files.

faq.question: What should I review before approving changes?
faq.answer: Review destination folders, deletion candidates, archive rules, naming changes, and any files marked as uncertain.
